A tall red band is the day CI broke across repositories, and Split by forge at the top stacks each result once per forge.

spec.expr: {container="forge-scout"} |= `scan ` | json msg="msg", forge="forge", scan_id="scan_id" | msg=`scan complete` or msg=`scan stopped` | forge=~"$forge" | keep scan_id

{container="forge-scout"} |= `security alert` | json msg="msg", forge="forge", scan_id="scan_id", forge_rank="forge_rank", connection="connection", repo="repo", severity="severity", rule="rule", tool="tool", number="number", url="url", created_at="created_at" | msg=`security alert` | forge=~"$forge" | forge_rank <= 200 | label_format repo=`{{ if eq .connection "$connections" }}{{ .repo }}{{ else }}{{ .repo }} on {{ .connection }}{{ end }}` | label_format link=`{{ if eq .forge "github" }}Open on GitHub{{ else if eq .forge "gitlab" }}Open on GitLab{{ else if eq .forge "gitea" }}Open on Gitea{{ else }}Open on Forgejo{{ end }}`

spec.title: Code scanning coverage
spec.description: How the newest scan covered code scanning on each GitHub connection. Not available counts repositories that never ran code scanning, and Unreadable those GitHub refused, which a missing permission causes. Cut short and Not sent count repositories with alerts left unread.

spec.expr: {container="forge-scout"} |= `scan ` | json msg="msg", forge="forge", scan_id="scan_id" | msg=`scan complete` or msg=`scan stopped` | forge=~"$forge" | keep scan_id

{container="forge-scout"} |= `scan ` | json msg="msg", forge="forge", connection="connection", scan_id="scan_id", security_alerts_read="security_alerts_read", security_repos_read="security_repos_read", security_skipped="security_skipped", security_unavailable="security_unavailable", security_unreadable="security_unreadable", security_truncated_repos="security_truncated_repos", security_unread_repos="security_unread_repos" | msg=`scan complete` or msg=`scan stopped` | forge=~"$forge" | security_alerts_read!=`unsupported`

defaults.noValue: No GitHub connection scanned in this range

spec.title: Scout status
spec.description: Running in green while any connection's newest scan line in the time range is younger than 3.5 times its scan_interval at the end of the range, whatever the Forge filter. Two scans can end 3.1 intervals apart, so a slow scan still reads Running. It turns red and reads Stalled when the scan loop, the container or the log pipeline stopped.

spec.expr: max(last_over_time({container="forge-scout"} |= `scan ` | json msg="msg", connection="connection", scan_interval_s="scan_interval_s" | msg=`scan complete` or msg=`scan stopped` | label_format fresh=`{{ if lt (mul 2 (sub ${__to:date:seconds} (unixEpoch __timestamp__))) (mul 7 .scan_interval_s) }}1{{ else }}0{{ end }}` | keep connection, fresh | unwrap fresh | __error__="" [$__range]) by (connection))

spec.title: Last scan per connection
spec.description: Every column reads each connection's newest scan in the time range. It shows when the scan started, whether it finished or stopped, the repositories it listed and skipped, the API budget left and whether it was degraded. A stopped scan lists no repositories, so those cells read -. Degraded scans in this range, below, counts the history.

spec.expr: last_over_time({container="forge-scout"} |= `scan ` | json msg="msg", forge="forge", connection="connection", scan_id="scan_id" | msg=`scan complete` or msg=`scan stopped` | forge=~"$forge" | label_format scan=`{{ if .scan_id }}{{ .scan_id }}{{ else }}NaN{{ end }}` | keep connection, forge, scan | unwrap scan | __error__="" [$__range]) by (connection, forge)

last_over_time({container="forge-scout"} |= `scan ` | json msg="msg", forge="forge", connection="connection" | msg=`scan complete` or msg=`scan stopped` | forge=~"$forge" | label_format ended=`{{ if .msg }}{{ if eq .msg "scan stopped" }}1{{ else }}0{{ end }}{{ else }}NaN{{ end }}` | keep connection, forge, ended | unwrap ended | __error__="" [$__range]) by (connection, forge)

last_over_time({container="forge-scout"} |= `scan ` | json msg="msg", forge="forge", connection="connection", repos_discovered="repos_discovered" | msg=`scan complete` or msg=`scan stopped` | forge=~"$forge" | label_format repos=`{{ if .repos_discovered }}{{ .repos_discovered }}{{ else }}NaN{{ end }}` | keep connection, forge, repos | unwrap repos | __error__="" [$__range]) by (connection, forge)

last_over_time({container="forge-scout"} |= `scan ` | json msg="msg", forge="forge", connection="connection", skipped="skipped" | msg=`scan complete` or msg=`scan stopped` | forge=~"$forge" | label_format skipped=`{{ if .skipped }}{{ .skipped }}{{ else }}NaN{{ end }}` | keep connection, forge, skipped | unwrap skipped | __error__="" [$__range]) by (connection, forge)

last_over_time({container="forge-scout"} |= `scan ` | json msg="msg", forge="forge", connection="connection", budget_remaining="budget_remaining" | msg=`scan complete` or msg=`scan stopped` | forge=~"$forge" | label_format budget=`{{ if .budget_remaining }}{{ .budget_remaining }}{{ else }}NaN{{ end }}` | keep connection, forge, budget | unwrap budget | __error__="" [$__range]) by (connection, forge)

last_over_time({container="forge-scout"} |= `scan ` | json msg="msg", forge="forge", connection="connection", degraded="degraded" | msg=`scan complete` or msg=`scan stopped` | forge=~"$forge" | label_format degraded=`{{ if .degraded }}{{ if eq .degraded "true" }}1{{ else }}0{{ end }}{{ else }}NaN{{ end }}` | keep connection, forge, degraded | unwrap degraded | __error__="" [$__range]) by (connection, forge)

spec.title: What the newest scan read
spec.description: The read state of every signal in each connection's newest scan. Partial means part of the signal is missing and Not read means none of it answered. Not reached means the scan stopped before it, and Not on this forge that the forge does not have it.

spec.expr: {container="forge-scout"} |= `scan ` | json msg="msg", forge="forge", scan_id="scan_id" | msg=`scan complete` or msg=`scan stopped` | forge=~"$forge" | keep scan_id

{container="forge-scout"} |= `scan ` | json msg="msg", forge="forge", connection="connection", scan_id="scan_id", repos_read="repos_read", open_prs_read="open_prs_read", open_issues_read="open_issues_read", runs_read="runs_read", failing_workflows_read="failing_workflows_read", pr_checks_read="pr_checks_read", security_alerts_read="security_alerts_read", disabled_workflows_read="disabled_workflows_read" | msg=`scan complete` or msg=`scan stopped` | forge=~"$forge"

spec.title: What connections cannot read
spec.description: One row per connection, from its newest scan in the time range, where Not on this forge names the signals the forge does not have. Empty owners names configured owners that resolved but listed no repository, often a typo or a token that cannot see them. The cut columns count repositories whose run, alert or workflow list stopped at a page limit, and Repo list cut reads Yes when the repository list itself was cut short. Checks not for this token counts the open pull requests whose checks GitHub refuses a fine-grained token, which a classic token with the repo scope reads.

spec.expr: {container="forge-scout"} |= `scan ` | json msg="msg", forge="forge", scan_id="scan_id" | msg=`scan complete` or msg=`scan stopped` | forge=~"$forge" | keep scan_id

{container="forge-scout"} |= `scan ` | json msg="msg", forge="forge", connection="connection", scan_id="scan_id", unsupported_signals="unsupported_signals", owners_empty="owners_empty", repos_truncated="repos_truncated", runs_truncated_repos="runs_truncated_repos", security_truncated_repos="security_truncated_repos", workflows_truncated_repos="workflows_truncated_repos", checks_unsupported_for_token="checks_unsupported_for_token" | msg=`scan complete` or msg=`scan stopped` | forge=~"$forge" | label_format unsupported_signals=`{{ .unsupported_signals | replace "_" " " | replace "," ", " }}`, owners_empty=`{{ .owners_empty | replace "," ", " }}`

spec.title: Scan problems
spec.description: Each degraded scan in the time range, newest first, up to 200, with its cause and what forge-scout logged. The cause names what to fix, such as a rejected token or a missing permission. Signals lists what the scan could not read whole.

spec.expr: {container="forge-scout"} |= `scan degraded` | json msg="msg", forge="forge", connection="connection", cause="cause", reason="reason", failed_signals="failed_signals" | msg=`scan degraded` | forge=~"$forge" | label_format signals=`{{ .failed_signals | replace "open_prs" "PRs" | replace "open_issues" "issues" | replace "pr_checks" "checks" | replace "security_alerts" "alerts" | replace "_" " " | replace "," ", " }}`

defaults.noValue: No degraded scans in this range

spec.title: Degraded scans in this range
spec.description: How many scans of each connection logged a degraded cause in the time range, the most first. One cause on many scans is a standing problem, such as a token that lost a permission. The Scan problems table below lists each scan.

spec.expr: sum by (connection, cause) (count_over_time({container="forge-scout"} |= `scan degraded` | json msg="msg", forge="forge", connection="connection", cause="cause" | msg=`scan degraded` | forge=~"$forge" [$__range]))

defaults.noValue: No degraded scans in this range

spec.title: Stopped scans per day by reason
spec.description: Scans that stopped before they finished, counted on the UTC day each stopped and stacked by reason. Budget reserve reached is forge-scout saving API budget for the next scan, which is working as intended. Rate limited and Scan ran past its limit need a look.

spec.expr: sum by (day, reason$split) (count_over_time({container="forge-scout"} |= `scan stopped` | json msg="msg", forge="forge", reason="reason" | msg=`scan stopped` | forge=~"$forge" | label_format day=`{{ (__timestamp__).UTC.Format "2006-01-02" }}` | label_format daystart=`{{ toDateInZone "2006-01-02" "UTC" .day | unixEpoch }}` | daystart >= ${__from:date:seconds} [$__range]))

defaults.noValue: No stopped scans in this range

spec.title: Runs coverage gaps
spec.description: Each time a repository's runs could not all be listed, newest first, up to 200. It happens after forge-scout was stopped for longer than its lookback, or when a list cut short skipped a run still in progress. Runs in the gap are never logged, and the failure streak after it is marked as starting at least that long ago.

spec.expr: {container="forge-scout"} |= `runs coverage gap` | json msg="msg", forge="forge", connection="connection", repo="repo", last_listed="last_listed", hours="hours", pending_since="pending_since" | msg=`runs coverage gap` | forge=~"$forge"

defaults.noValue: No coverage gap in this range

spec.title: API budget left per connection
spec.description: The API budget each connection's forge reported after its scan, lowest per interval. A line that reaches the bottom before each reset means scans are too frequent for the budget. Gitea and Forgejo report no budget.

spec.expr: min by (connection) (min_over_time({container="forge-scout"} |= `scan ` | json msg="msg", forge="forge", connection="connection", budget_remaining="budget_remaining" | msg=`scan complete` or msg=`scan stopped` | forge=~"$forge" | unwrap budget_remaining | __error__="" [$__interval]) by (connection))

defaults.noValue: No budget reported in this range

spec.title: Scan length per connection
spec.description: How long each connection's scan took, from its first read to its save, longest per interval. A rising line on one connection points at a slow forge or a growing number of repositories.

spec.expr: max by (connection) (max_over_time({container="forge-scout"} |= `scan complete` | json msg="msg", forge="forge", connection="connection", duration_ms="duration_ms" | msg=`scan complete` | forge=~"$forge" | unwrap duration_ms | __error__="" [$__interval]) by (connection))

spec.title: Failed reads per day by signal
spec.description: Each finished or stopped scan that could not read a signal whole counts once under that signal, on the UTC day it ended, so a scan that failed two signals adds to both bands. A band that comes back every day names a signal that keeps failing. No bars means no scan failed a read, and Stopped scans per day by reason shows the stops. Split by forge at the top stacks each signal once per forge.

sum by (day, signal$split) (count_over_time({container="forge-scout"} |= `scan ` | json msg="msg", forge="forge", degraded="degraded", failed_signals="failed_signals" | msg=`scan complete` or msg=`scan stopped` | forge=~"$forge" | degraded=`true` | failed_signals=~`(.*,)?failing_workflows(,.*)?` | label_format signal=`failing_workflows` | label_format day=`{{ (__timestamp__).UTC.Format "2006-01-02" }}` | label_format daystart=`{{ toDateInZone "2006-01-02" "UTC" .day | unixEpoch }}` | daystart >= ${__from:date:seconds} [$__range]))
